hooks.text: Emergency push-bar doors were not designed for simple convenience.
Every push-bar emergency exit exists because of an 1883 child stampede.
In 1883, 183 children died behind a bolted hall door.

title: How an 1883 Child Disaster Created Emergency Doors 🤯
description: In 1883, a rush for free toys at Victoria Hall in Sunderland turned fatal when an inward-opening door was bolted nearly shut. The tragedy killed 183 children and permanently changed emergency exit design worldwide.

beats.text: Emergency push-bar doors were not designed for simple convenience.

beats.text: In 1883, over eleven hundred children packed Victoria Hall in Sunderland.
beats.visual: engraving of Victoria Hall building in Sunderland, 1883

beats.text: Free toys were promised, triggering a rush down the stairs.

queries: Illustrated London News Victoria Hall Sunderland

beats.text: At the bottom, an inward door was bolted open one child wide.

queries: Victoria Hall disaster bolted door diagram

beats.text: Trapped against it, 183 children suffocated in the stairs.

beats.text: The disaster forced new laws creating push-bar emergency exits.

beats.text: Public safety doors were born from disaster, not convenience.
